# package emcy

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/emcy"
```

Package emcy implements the CANopen emergency object (CiA 301 7.2.7).

A [Producer](#type-producer) is a node's side: [Producer.Raise](#func-producer-raise) records an error (active error set, error register 0x1001, pre-defined error field 0x1003) and sends its emergency message; [Producer.Clear](#func-producer-clear) deactivates it and sends the error reset message (0x0000) once no error remains. The COB-ID (0x1014, whose invalid bit suppresses the messages) and the inhibit time (0x1015, in 100 µs units) come from options or from the node's dictionary; messages within the inhibit time are delayed, not lost.

A [Consumer](#type-consumer) receives the emergency messages of all nodes (or of given COB-IDs) and reports them as [Event](#type-event) values.

#### CANopen FD {#hdr-CANopen_FD}

CiA 1301 replaces the 8-byte message by a 20-byte one ([FDMessage](#type-fdmessage)): logical device number, CiA specification number of the error code, the classical code, register and 5 device-specific bytes, a status byte and a TIME\_OF\_DAY time stamp, on the same COB-ID (default 080h + node-ID). [WithFD](#func-withfd) makes a producer send it and a consumer accept it. Sources: CiA's CANopen FD poster (CiA 1301, field list with byte positions, 2026 edition), the HMS/Ixxat "Basics of the CANopen and CANopen FD protocol" whitepaper (same fields, and an error status state machine), CiA's "EMCY write protocol" page (field meanings) and its CAN Newsletter article on logical devices in CANopen FD (20 bytes). The poster places the EEC in bytes 4..5 and the register in byte 6; the whitepaper the register in byte 4 and the EEC in 5..6: FDLayoutCiA (default) and FDLayoutRegisterFirst select between them. The status encoding and the byte order of the CiA specification number are not public (raw byte; little-endian assumed).

[CodeText](#func-codetext) describes the error codes of CiA 301 table 21, and [ErrorRegister](#type-errorregister) names the error register bits.

Long-running services have Start, which subscribes before it returns, and Close, which stops them and waits for their goroutine. Callbacks run on the service's goroutine and must not block for long.

Emergency error codes of CiA 301 (table 21). The low byte of a generic code (xx00) is free for device profiles and manufacturers; [CodeText](#func-codetext) falls back to the class of such codes.

```go
const FDSize = 20
```

FDSize is the payload length of a CANopen FD emergency message (CiA 1301 EMCY write protocol): 20 bytes, a valid CAN FD length.

## Functions

### func CodeText

```go
func CodeText(code uint16) string
```

CodeText describes an emergency error code after CiA 301 table 21. A code the table does not list is described by its class (0x8113 as "CAN overrun (objects lost)", 0x2310 as "current, device output side", 0x5432 as "device hardware, generic error"), with the code in parentheses when it is not exactly the listed one.

### func ParseFDFrame

```go
func ParseFDFrame(f *canbus.Frame, l FDLayout) (m Message, fd *FDMessage, err error)
```

ParseFDFrame decodes an emergency frame of a CANopen FD network: a CAN FD data frame of at least FDSize bytes is a CANopen FD message (fd is non-nil, and m its classical part); a classical frame, or a CAN FD frame of up to 8 bytes, is decoded as [ParseMessage](#func-parsemessage) does.

### type ErrorRegister

```go
type ErrorRegister uint8
```

ErrorRegister is the error register (object 0x1001), sent in every emergency message.

```go
const (
	RegGeneric       ErrorRegister = 1 << 0
	RegCurrent       ErrorRegister = 1 << 1
	RegVoltage       ErrorRegister = 1 << 2
	RegTemperature   ErrorRegister = 1 << 3
	RegCommunication ErrorRegister = 1 << 4 // overrun, error state
	RegDeviceProfile ErrorRegister = 1 << 5 // device profile specific
	RegReserved      ErrorRegister = 1 << 6 // always 0
	RegManufacturer  ErrorRegister = 1 << 7 // manufacturer-specific
)
```

Error register bits (CiA 301 7.5.2.2). RegGeneric is set whenever any error is active.

### type FDLayout

```go
type FDLayout uint8
```

FDLayout selects the byte positions of the error register and the emergency error code in a CANopen FD emergency message. The public sources disagree on them (see the package documentation), so the layout is selectable; every other field has the same position in both.

```go
const (
	// FDLayoutCiA (the default) follows CiA's CANopen FD poster (CiA 1301,
	// 2026 edition): EEC in bytes 4..5, error register in byte 6, so that
	// bytes 4..11 are the classical 8-byte emergency message.
	FDLayoutCiA FDLayout = iota
	// FDLayoutRegisterFirst follows the HMS/Ixxat CANopen FD whitepaper:
	// error register in byte 4, EEC in bytes 5..6.
	FDLayoutRegisterFirst
)
```

CANopen FD emergency layouts.

### type FDMessage

```go
type FDMessage struct {
	LogicalDevice uint8
	CiASpec       uint16
	Code          uint16
	Register      ErrorRegister
	Specific      [5]byte
	Status        uint8
	Time          timestamp.TimeOfDay
}
```

FDMessage is the content of a CANopen FD emergency message (CiA 1301 EMCY write protocol), 20 bytes:

	byte  0      logical device number
	byte  1      reserved (0)
	bytes 2..3   CiA specification number defining the EEC
	bytes 4..5   emergency error code (EEC)        } FDLayoutCiA; with
	byte  6      error register (object 1001h)     } FDLayoutRegisterFirst
	                                                 register 4, EEC 5..6
	bytes 7..11  device-specific error information
	byte  12     status (type of error)
	byte  13     reserved (0)
	bytes 14..19 time (TIME_OF_DAY)

Multi-byte fields are little-endian, as all CANopen values; the sources do not state it for this message. The encoding of Status ("type of error, e.g. recoverable/non recoverable") is not public: it is carried as a raw byte.

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*config)
```

Option configures a [Producer](#type-producer) or a [Consumer](#type-consumer). Each option names the services it applies to; the others ignore it.

#### func WithCOBID

```go
func WithCOBID(cob canopen.COBID) Option
```

WithCOBID sets the COB-ID of a [Producer](#type-producer) (default 0x80 + node-ID, or 0x1014 with a dictionary). A COB-ID with [canopen.COBInvalid](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#COBInvalid) set disables the transmission; errors are still recorded.

#### func WithDictionary

```go
func WithDictionary(d *od.Dictionary) Option
```

WithDictionary makes a [Producer](#type-producer) use a node's object dictionary: the COB-ID EMCY (0x1014) and the inhibit time (0x1015) are read from it and followed when written, the error register 0x1001 and, when the object exists, the pre-defined error field 0x1003 are kept up to date. The write hooks it installs refuse a new CAN-ID in 0x1014 while the COB-ID is valid, and any value but 0 in 0x1003:0 (writing 0 clears the error history), with [canopen.AbortInvalidValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#AbortInvalidValue).

#### func WithFD

```go
func WithFD(brs bool) Option
```

WithFD selects CANopen FD (CiA 1301). A [Producer](#type-producer) sends 20-byte CAN FD emergency messages ([FDMessage](#type-fdmessage); bit rate switching when brs is true) built from the classical fields and the [WithFDInfo](#func-withfdinfo) and [WithFDClock](#func-withfdclock) values; a [Consumer](#type-consumer) also accepts CAN FD frames and reports CANopen FD messages in [Event.FD](#func-event-fd) (without the option it counts CAN FD frames as invalid).

### type Producer

```go
type Producer struct {

	// orders dictionary updates

	// the dictionary has 0x1003

	// removes the dictionary hooks

}
```

Producer is a node's emergency producer (CiA 301 7.2.7). It keeps the set of active errors and the error register derived from it, records every raised error in the error history (newest first), and sends emergency messages: one per newly raised error and an error reset (code 0x0000) when the last active error is cleared.

Consecutive messages are at least the inhibit time apart; messages that come sooner are queued in order and sent when the inhibit time has passed (up to 256 queued messages; Start runs the queue). Without an inhibit time and with an empty queue, messages are sent synchronously by the calling goroutine.

NewProducer returns the emergency producer of a node. ```go

Clear deactivates an error. When no error remains active it sends the error reset message (code 0x0000, register 0); otherwise it only updates the register. Clearing an error that is not active does nothing.

#### func (Producer) Raise

```go
func (p *Producer) Raise(ctx context.Context, code uint16, reg ErrorRegister, msef [5]byte) error
```

Raise records an error and sends its emergency message: the error becomes active, the register (0x1001) includes reg and the generic bit, and the code is added to the history (0x1003, newest at sub-index 1; the upper 16 bits of an entry, manufacturer-specific additional information, are 0). Raising an error that is already active only adds reg to its register bits: no message, no history entry. Code 0x0000 is refused.


Register returns the error register.

#### func (Producer) Send

```go
func (p *Producer) Send(ctx context.Context, m Message) error
```

Send sends an emergency message as it is, without changing the active errors, the register or the history. It is queued when the inhibit time has not passed since the previous message, and sent at once (returning the bus error) otherwise. A COB-ID with the invalid bit set suppresses it. A producer made [WithFD](#func-withfd) sends it as a CANopen FD message.


SendFD sends a CANopen FD emergency message as it is (in a CAN FD frame, whether or not the producer was made [WithFD](#func-withfd)), as [Producer.Send](#func-producer-send) does.
